`hB` is an explicit binder of the theorem. Nothing else in the statement mentions it: `B` is a separate implicit binder, and `htrace` and the conclusion only use `B`. So the statement still elaborates without `hB`.

The proof uses `hB` only in the two calls `setIntegral_congr_ae (hB.prod measurableSet_Ioc)`. In both calls the integrands agree at every point.
- `hleft`: the membership `hqmem` is introduced but never used. The step only rewrites with `hτsymm` (proved for all q), `parabolicHomeomorph_symm_apply` (true by `rfl`, Topology.lean:105) and `buGaussian_timeShift_point_symm_apply σ z` (BUGaussianTimeShift.lean:57, holds for all σ and z).
- `hright`: `F (τprod.symm (τprod q)) = F q` holds for every q, by `simp`.

So both calls can be replaced by `integral_congr_ae` with `filter_upwards [] with q`. `setIntegral_parabolic_to_product` already uses exactly this pattern.

The rest of the proof does not need `B` to be measurable:
- `MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_image_emb` (Mathlib, Bochner/Set.lean:572) takes any `s : Set X`. It needs only measure preservation and a measurable embedding.
- `himage` is purely set-theoretic.
- `setIntegral_parabolic_to_product` (ParabolicMeasure.lean:54) has no measurability hypothesis on Ω or I.

The statement is also true for any B: translating time is a measure-preserving measurable embedding, so the two set integrals are equal for every set B. The hypothesis can be deleted.
